nodes.name: Cu foam precleaning
nodes.procedure: Cu foam was ultrasonically cleaned in 20% sulfuric acid solution for 5 min and cleaned with DI water for several times.
nodes.source_text: Firstly, Cu foam was ultrasonically cleaned in 20% sulfuric acid solution for 5 min and cleaned with DI water for several times.

nodes.name: Cu(OH)2 nanorods fabrication
nodes.procedure: 30 ml NaOH aqueous solution (4M) was slowly poured into 30 ml NH4S2O8 solution (0.12M). Then the mixed solution was stirred evenly. The cleaned Cu foam was immersed into the mixed solution at room temperature for 35 min, and the Cu surface completely converted to blue. Finally, the converted Cu foam was washed with DI water for several times and dried in oven at 60°C.

nodes.name: Cu2S nanorods fabrication
nodes.procedure: 1mmol Na2S was dissolved into 35 ml DI water. The converted Cu foam with Cu(OH)2 coating was immersed into the solution. After hydrothermal reaction at 120°C for 5 h, Cu2S precursor was obtained after washed with DI water and ethanol and then dried at 60°C.

nodes.name: Cu2O nanorods fabrication
nodes.procedure: The Cu(OH)2 array was annealed at 400°C for 120 min in N2 atmosphere.
nodes.source_text: The Cu2O nanorods was prepared through annealing Cu(OH)2 array at 400°C for 120 min in N2 atmosphere.

nodes.name: Cu2S@Ni electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: The solution for deposition was prepared with 0.017M NiSO4, 0.016M sodium citrate and 0.285M NaCl in 180 ml DI water. Then the pH of solution was adjusted to 8.5 with ammonia. The process of deposition was carried out at 40°C under heating in water bath. The Cu2S precursor was coated with nickel by constant potential deposition at -2.5V for 1 h in a three-electrode system. The saturated calomel electrode (SCE) and graphite paper acted as reference electrode and counter electrode, respectively. After the deposition, the catalysts were washed with DI water and dried at 60°C in vacuum oven.

nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 1a demonstrates that the Cu(OH)₂ nanorods uniformly covered the Cu foam surface... nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms Cu(OH)₂ phase after etching (16.7°, 23.8°, 34.1° etc.), Cu₂S phase after sulfurization (27.9°, 30.3°, 32.8° etc.), and metallic Ni peaks (44.5°, 51.8°, 76.4°) in Cu₂S@Ni.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After impregnation etching, the obvious signals at 16.7°, 23.8°, 34.1°, 35.9°, 39.8° and 53.2° can be indexed to the reported Cu(OH)₂. When the material was sulfurized by Na₂S, the diffraction peaks obviously changed... peaks appear at 27.9°, 30.3°, 32.8°... Compared to the signals of Cu₂S, there are new signals at 44.5°, 51.8° and 76.4°.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectrum of Cu₂S@Ni shows peaks at 282 and 332 cm⁻¹ attributed to Ni-S vibrations indicating strong Cu₂S-Ni interaction; Cu₂S and Cu₂O@Ni shown for comparison.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 2b, Cu₂S@Ni exhibits obvious peaks at 282 and 332 cm⁻¹ which could be attributed to the Ni-S vibrations, indicating a strong interaction between the Cu₂S core and surface Ni.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution XPS Ni 2p of Cu₂S@Ni shows Ni 2p₃/₂ peaks at 852.7 eV (Ni⁰) and 856.2 eV (Ni²⁺), Ni 2p₁/₂ at 870.2 eV (Ni⁰) and 873.7 eV (Ni²⁺).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni 2p₃/₂ peaks of Cu₂S@Ni splitting at 852.7 and 856.2 eV can be assigned to the Ni⁰ and Ni²⁺ states, respectively, while the Ni 2p₁/₂ at 870.2 and 873.7 eV can also correspond to Ni⁰ and Ni²⁺...
